A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VISTA3D and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, algorithms, and supplementary material. The changed title, layout, and relocated content do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 Sections 4–6 and the supplement report original segmentation benchmarks, zero-shot experiments, ablations, and fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds SAM2 fine-tuning comparisons, runtime measurements, and qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The backbone, two branches, supervoxel generation, merging algorithm, and four-stage training are retained. However, v2 Section 3.2 specifies a two-convolution post-mapping layer P, whereas v3 omits P and describes the feature as decoder output. The PDFs do not establish whether this component was removed or absorbed into a simplified description.

E1.justification: v3 adds fluid-around-kidney segmentation as a qualitative zero-shot target (supplementary Figure 12). The training inventory, principal benchmark cohorts, and fine-tuning tasks remain unchanged; the new SAM2 experiments reuse TotalSegmentatorV2 and MSD Task07.

E2.justification: v3 adds fine-tuned SAM2 as a substantive comparator for supported-class interactive segmentation on TotalSegmentatorV2 and MSD Task07 (supplementary Section 3.3, Figure 4, and Table 2). MedSAM and SegVol also participate in new hepatic-vessel and pancreas qualitative comparisons. The earlier principal comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include SAM2 training with axial slices treated as video frames, 500 epochs on eight A100 GPUs for TotalSegmentator, and center-slice foreground prompting. v3 also introduces timing across four volume sizes resampled to 1.5 mm on a 16GB V100, plus lower-memory tests. Existing data splits and patch-based benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted case studies of one-pixel boundary editing, difficult hepatic-vessel/pancreas segmentation, and erroneous organ predictions when clicking nearby fluid, plus a SAM2 convergence curve. The supervoxel ablation, liver-substructure embedding example, and shared-encoder/decoder pilot discussion already appeared in v2.

E5.justification: v3 supplementary Figure 4 introduces a shaded band around the SAM2 curve, but neither its caption nor the text defines the band or its estimation procedure. Neither PDF specifies repeated-run or seed counts. Whether the band constitutes newly reported statistical uncertainty cannot be determined reliably.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark tables, per-class appendix values, fine-tuning scores, and zero-shot curves are unchanged. v3 adds SAM2 results, including pancreas/tumor Dice of 0.557/0.308 alongside VISTA3D's retained 0.802/0.603, and new qualitative findings. New runtime results include 1m07s versus 4m34s at 333×333×603 on a 16GB V100 for default 118-class VISTA3D and 117-class TotalSegmentator segmentation.

T1.justification: The segmentation-logit expression, connected-component construction, and SAM-feature/SLIC formulation show no substantive mathematical revision. Pseudocode compaction does not add theoretical reasoning, and neither version presents formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central automatic segmentation, interactive editing, zero-shot, and transfer-learning claims remain. v3 explicitly emphasizes priority as the first unified workflow model and newly claims a 50% zero-shot improvement from supervoxels in the introduction, refining the quantitative and novelty claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds spatial-versus-temporal reasoning about SAM2 and expands interpretation of organ overfitting. It removes v2's explicit CT-only and supervoxel limitations, including conservative predictions and failures on large whole-body objects. The fine-tuning discussion also replaces the plateau qualification with emphasis on a favorable WORD ranking, materially changing the balance of interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: The new Computational Details section reports 64 32GB V100 GPUs, approximately 20,000 GPU hours, interactive prompt counts, memory requirements, and adaptive CPU/GPU inference. v3 also discloses embedding width, additional click-sampling and baseline-training details, and identifies MAISI as the synthetic-data generator. These expand documentation without establishing corresponding changes to existing experiments; VISTA3D code/weights access remains the same.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops positioning against SAM2, SAM3D, and 3DSAM-Adapter, and adds references including Medical Vision Generalist, One-Prompt, and MAISI. SAM-Med2D and SAM-Med3D references are removed. SAT receives expanded discussion but was already cited under its paper title in v2.

P1.justification: The title changes, and the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around the unified annotation workflow and the distinction between 2D/video and 3D medical segmentation. Related work and the conclusion are substantially revised, while the supplement is reorganized around computational details, training, examples, and discussion.

P2.justification: v3 switches to a two-column layout and replaces the simple architecture diagram with a detailed workflow/model figure. Several existing qualitative figures move into the main text, while the mouse example and left-lung plot move into the supplement. New timing tables, SAM2 plots, and qualitative panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added SAM2 experiments and explicit training/inference costs strengthen assessment of the 3D design and practical feasibility, while the revised workflow figure improves clarity. Core results remain unchanged. These benefits are tempered by removal of specific supervoxel/large-object limitations and incomplete explanation of the new SAM2 plot, supporting a limited net improvement.
